facts.raw_span: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
afebrile
blood pressure was 110/80 mmHg
firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
carcinoembryonic antigen 1.14 ng/mL
CA-125 21 U/mL
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor
double inferior vena cava was identified, with the left cava draining via the left renal vein to the right-sided cava

concepts.why: The patient presents with a right adnexal mass and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa, which is concerning for an ovarian neoplasm.
The patient has multiple uterine fibroids, which are visible on transvaginal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis.
The patient has lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora, which is consistent with lymphedema.
The patient has a double inferior vena cava, which is an anatomical variation that can be identified on imaging studies.
The patient presents with a firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant, which is consistent with an adnexal mass.
The patient has a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor, which is based on the imaging findings and clinical presentation.
The patient has a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion in the abdominopelvic region, which is visible on contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis.
The patient has lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora, which is consistent with unilateral lymphedema.

rationales.F01: Right lower abdominal pain is a common symptom of ovarian neoplasms.
rationales.F02: Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora is a characteristic feature of unilateral lymphedema.
rationales.F05: A firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant is suggestive of an adnexal mass.
rationales.F09: Transvaginal ultrasound showing multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa supports the diagnosis of uterine fibroids and an adnexal mass.
rationales.F10: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealing a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion is highly suggestive of an ovarian neoplasm.
rationales.F11: A provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor is based on the imaging findings and clinical presentation.
rationales.F12: A double inferior vena cava is a rare anatomical variation that can be incidentally identified on imaging studies.
